stories.title: Google Begins Paying Publishers for AI Overview Answers
stories.simple_summary: Google is starting to pay news organizations money when Google's AI tools use their articles to answer questions for people searching online.
stories.why_it_matters: If you run a news website or blog, this could eventually mean getting paid when AI systems use your content, similar to how newspapers share ad money.

stories.title: Emotionally Intelligent People Use a Simple 3-Word Phrase to Guide Their Approach to A.I.
stories.simple_summary: An article suggests that emotionally intelligent people use a simple 3-word phrase to guide how they approach AI.
stories.why_it_matters: This is general advice about mindset rather than news about AI itself — it's mostly motivational rather than something that changes how AI works.

stories.title: Trump's meeting with tech leaders leaves AI safety more unsettled than ever
stories.simple_summary: After President Trump met with technology leaders, there's uncertainty about what the government will do to make sure AI systems stay safe and don't cause harm.
stories.why_it_matters: Government decisions about AI safety could eventually affect what features are available in tools you use, but nothing concrete has changed yet.

stories.title: Trump signs executive order rebranding AI as 'Super Intelligence' as tech titans ink separate SI accord
stories.simple_summary: President Trump signed an order telling the government to start calling AI "Super Intelligence" instead, and some tech companies agreed to use that term too.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mainly a naming change in official documents — it doesn't change how AI actually works or how you'd use it.

stories.title: Sam Altman says OpenAI won’t go public until its models are safe
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI's leader says the company won't sell stock to the public (go public) until they're confident their AI systems are safe enough.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors thinking about the company's future — it doesn't affect you unless you're considering investing in OpenAI.

stories.title: America.gov gets really weird when you ask it about Minecraft, but it’s not a glitch
stories.simple_summary: The government's website (America.gov) gives strange answers when asked about Minecraft, the video game, but this is actually intentional for security reasons rather than a mistake.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a quirky technical detail that doesn't affect everyday people using government websites for actual information.

stories.title: OpenAI Ignored Employees’ Warnings About Safely Testing A.I. Models
stories.simple_summary: According to reports, OpenAI's own employees warned the company about safety risks before testing new AI models, but the company moved forward anyway.
stories.why_it_matters: This suggests OpenAI may not have been as careful as it could be when releasing new AI — it's worth knowing if you depend on their products.

stories.title: Trump orders US government to call AI ‘Super Intelligence’
stories.simple_summary: President Trump signed an order requiring the US government to use the term "Super Intelligence" instead of "artificial intelligence" in all official documents and websites.
stories.why_it_matters: This is just a word change in government paperwork — it doesn't change how AI tools actually work or how you'd use them.

stories.title: The internet is convinced Elon Musk’s xAI trolled OpenAI’s ‘Dots’ launch
stories.simple_summary: Elon Musk's AI company (xAI) bought the domain name dot.com right before OpenAI launched a new product called "Dots," which some people think was a intentional prank.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly corporate drama between tech companies — it doesn't affect regular people using AI tools.

stories.title: Elon Musk’s AI-powered Grokipedia is updating again
stories.simple_summary: Elon Musk's AI-powered encyclopedia (Grokipedia) has started updating its articles again after being paused for several months.
stories.why_it_matters: Unless you regularly use Grokipedia as a reference, this is mainly interesting to tech enthusiasts — it doesn't impact most people.

stories.title: OpenAI DevDay recap: AI lab rolls out Dots agents, Altman and Friar comment on IPO
stories.simple_summary: OpenAI announced new AI agents (software that can do tasks for you) at a developer conference, and leaders discussed the company's future stock offering plans.
stories.why_it_matters: The new AI agents might eventually help businesses automate work, but the stock offering plans mainly matter to investors.

stories.title: Will A.I. Make Your Brain Lazy? Here’s What the New Research Actually Shows.
stories.simple_summary: A news article explores research about whether using AI tools might make people's brains less active or lazy over time.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a discussion about the long-term effects of relying on AI, which is worth thinking about if you start using these tools regularly.
